heard_on_the_hill.headline: Lawmakers renew request for Huang to brief Congress
heard_on_the_hill.body: Chairmen Mast, Moolenaar and Crawford sent a second request on November 13 asking Jensen Huang and Nvidia to "Brief Congress on the Chinese Intelligence Asset." Moolenaar had said he would look to subpoena Huang if they could not agree on a date, per POLITICO, and later said Huang agreed to closed-door testimony with a date still pending, Lianhe Zaobao reported.

heard_on_the_hill.tag: House Select Committee on the CCP, November 13
heard_on_the_hill.headline: Select Committee releases report on U.S. manufacturing
heard_on_the_hill.body: Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) released a bipartisan report on November 13 on "How China Undermined Western Manufacturing and Helped Hollow Out American Industry." It focuses on four case studies: the biomanufacturing, aerospace, semiconductor and machine tool industries.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Democrats press Lutnick on Nvidia chip approvals
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senators Warren and Coons on November 11 directed Lutnick, Rubio and Miller to preserve Nvidia records, and on November 12 Wyden and Neal began investigating what they called an "Administration Scheme to Take Cut of Nvidia AI Chip Sales to Chinese Companies." Lutnick has reportedly agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on the administration's approval of Nvidia chip exports to China, CNBC reports.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Cantwell urges Lutnick to halt AI chip sales to China
heard_on_the_hill.body: Sen. Maria Cantwell, the top Democrat on the Senate Commerce Committee, sent Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick a letter on Sunday, November 15, telling him "You Failed to Protect National Security & America's Tech Edge." CNBC reported she urged him to halt AI chip sales to China ahead of this week's Trump-Xi summit.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Johnson sees consensus for tighter China chip curbs
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Speaker Mike Johnson told reporters on November 12 there is a developing consensus in Congress to limit China's access to advanced AI chips, per the Taipei Times. Congressional Republicans want to attach new chip-export restrictions to the annual defense authorization bill, with lawmakers pushing at least four separate bills on chip exports.
